terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static fence panel that tiles post to post. Both faces are seen and nothing is hollow, but nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A level builder places these in runs of dozens, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. ONE POST PER TILE: the post sits on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain post-bay-post-bay along X with no doubled post at a joint. The universal Thai construction hoarding, seen in runs of dozens around every condo site. Pale blue paint chalked to the zinc at the ribs, rust from every screw, torn posters and a sprayed phone number near the base.

reasoning: A 3 x 1.85 m welded 50 mm square-tube frame (top, bottom and mid rail, a short +X upright) IN FRONT of a vertically corrugated sheet, whose -X upright IS the 60 mm ground post, standing in the frame plane from the ground to 0.10 m above the top rail as the plate shows (proxy: posts alone at 0.00-0.14 H, frame and sheet 0.20-0.98 H, mid rail at 0.53 of the frame height on the front depth map).

Three materials: the pale blue sheet with a chalk-and-rust-streak canvas, the galvanised steel with a rust canvas, and an alpha-cut paper pane for the paste-ups and spray stencil -- a printed graphic is the post-construction canvas case.

The 40 ribs are ONE extruded sine profile carrying crest and valley vertex tones, so the corrugation is geometry that catches light and gives the wavy top edge, at ~3,400 triangles; the 60 screw heads along the three rails are ONE InstancedMesh -- the fourth draw call of four.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the frame root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the ribbed pale-blue sheet inside a dark frame with posters at the base; the ribs are the silhouette of the top edge and have to be geometry, the rest is canvas.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 3.00 x 2.40 x 0.12 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.

Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static fence geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: one proxy over the whole panel envelope, which is what a run of fence collides as.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. reviewHistory.summary: Surface pass: paint canvas on the sheet with rust runs from all three rail lines, mottle and grain; rust canvas on the frame; poster canvas on the pane.
Lighting pass: no rim light and no contact shadow in the plate; both recorded absent. Exposure 1.0, ACES filmic; the ribs shade themselves under the key.

Interaction pass: ONE root pivot, ZERO sockets, one BOX collider on the frame root, no destruction groups; a hand compound of three boxes (sheet, frame, post) at coverage 0.994 after the derivation covered 0.81.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 3,906/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, three canvases at 3.0 MB, factory ~75 ms. Turntable: 0/180 segment at ~0.43 of frame; 90/270 are UNSEGMENTABLE by size (a 0.13 m sliver, ~2% of frame against the segmenter's 3.5% floor), recorded as a gate limitation of every 3 m panel.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 4.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,906 of 4,000: the 40-rib sine ribbon is ~3,400 of them.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Tinted boxes for the frame and post, one closed sine-profile extrusion for the sheet, one quad for the posters, one InstancedMesh of screw heads.
One InstancedMesh: 60 screw heads. The ribs are one profile, not 40 parts.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Three canvases after construction (512 paint, 256 rust, 512 poster), 3.0 MB of texture VRAM; factory ~75 ms.

risks.description: At 90 and 270 degrees the panel is a 0.13 m sliver at a 1.93 m framing radius, about 2% of the frame; the turntable segmenter needs 3.5% and reports those azimuths unsegmented.
risks.mitigation: A property of every 3 m panel, not of this build: the 0 and 180 captures segment at 0.43 / 0.41 of frame and the 90/270 renders show the sliver. Recorded, not bypassed.

risks.description: The proxy is squarer (w/h 1.03) than the declared 1.25, so the band table reads a 0.186 width residual.
risks.mitigation: The declared envelope is built; reported as the declared aspect.

risks.description: The stencil text is a generic sans, not a real spray stencil face.
risks.mitigation: Read at prop distance as a sprayed number; recorded.
